quicksilver: Mercury; used figuratively for something rapid, volatile, or elusive.
tokenizer: A component that splits text into discrete tokens (integer IDs).
embedding: A learned mapping from a discrete token to a continuous vector.
softmax: A function that turns a vector of scores into a probability distribution summing to one.
attention: A mechanism that weighs tokens by learned relevance to one another.
quantization: Reducing the numeric precision of weights to save memory and compute.
superposition: Storing many near-orthogonal features in fewer dimensions than features.
nucleus: In sampling, the smallest high-probability set of tokens covering a target mass.
temperature: A scalar that sharpens or flattens a probability distribution before sampling.
vocabulary: The complete set of tokens a model can read or emit.
disperses: Spreads or scatters something across a range.
manifold: A space that locally resembles ordinary Euclidean space; here, a high-dimensional feature space.
